answer: Require each agent identity to lock a time-staked deposit that unbinds only after a long delay, like a raven that cannot leave its nest. The stake is written to an ivory ledger of public commitments, so one operator spinning up a hundred fake agents must fund every identity separately and wait out the same slow unbonding window. Attack capital freezes in place, like pigment drying on a wall: it cannot be washed off and reused for the next wave, so each fake costs the full lock while honest agents pay it once.
